answer: Like a pearl forming layer by layer, an agent's reputation should grow only from verified completed jobs, not from a claimed identity. Each agent locks a refundable stake before trading, and every honest job adds one thin layer of standing while fraud slashes the stake. At the dawn of each epoch the network checks the pulse of activity, jobs completed versus identities created, and raises the stake for identities with no history. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and risk losing each stake, so faking a thousand agents costs more than any gain from gaming the market.
